target: Smooth 60 fps on live vlang.io; still open
scope: Changed native layer contents after updateLayer, with changed scroll position; entire first-to-last input period. Not physical display scanout.

protocol.title: V — The V Programming Language
protocol.profile_cache: Fresh empty private profile/cache; direct HTTPS; automatic author scripts; OS filesystem/shader caches retained.

policies.exit_lifetime: Default: keep main prealloc arena alive through normal process termination while detached workers still run; ordinary scope and worker retirement stays active.
policies.regional_recorder: Off: both mean pairs improve, first p95 regresses slightly; later target reuse is mixed.
policies.regional_target: Off: 89.39 to 92.96 and 92.13 to 90.51 fps; p95 and maxima remain outside the target.
policies.single_wait: Off: 88.70 to 88.03 and 88.41 to 91.03 fps; first p95 worsens, both maxima worsen.
policies.font_leases: Off: 78.07 to 89.74 and 90.06 to 96.23 fps; p95 improves, second maximum worsens. Input diagnostic confirms token encoding/decoding and immutable identity reuse.
policies.gradient_input_deferral: Off: 79.60 to 90.31 and 91.19 to 90.82 fps. Input diagnostic confirms eight completed groups and 16 omitted leaves, maximum pixel error two. Second p95 and maximum regress.
policies.combined_gpu: Off: compatible flags pass the existing three-level pixel bound, but pairs 87.31 to 75.95 and 88.22 to 89.92 fps are mixed.
policies.expired_frame_timers: Off: zero expired timers skipped during the input window; ineligible, no timing arms. Native ARC/MRC tests cover conservative same-view and deadline semantics.
policies.bounded_parallel_lanes: Off: input jobs use at most two lanes, so the four-lane cap cannot bind. Exact scheduler, pixel and sanitizer tests pass; no FPS credit.
policies.parallel_readback_rows: Off: zero channel-swap-rows jobs during input; the large copies occur at startup. No timing arms. Exact native and sanitizer checks pass. Six alternating conversion microbenchmarks improve median 105.43 to 61.59 microseconds at 1174x1242 and 448.35 to 211.39 microseconds at 3416x1906; not scrolling measurements.

limitations: Native publications do not establish physical display scanout. Mean throughput above 60 does not establish smooth 60 fps.
All complete pairs and failed attempts are retained. Host load is recorded per run; variation and contention limit causal attribution.
The first Dawn recorder diagnostic exited with an incomplete log; no credit. The first target diagnostic completed inputs then faulted in the detached HTTP reaper during shutdown; invalid.

A first exit interposer recursively resolved exit and was stopped. Full raw output survives as browser.log.gz with separately verified original SHA256. Its corrected follow-up changed bundle identity mid-run and is invalid.
A deterministic prealloc regression reproduces the original teardown fault, then checks five normal fresh-process browser-policy exits. Subsequent live cohorts complete normally.

The initial gradient-input fixture lacked a configured default font, then reused stale clip state between simulated frames. A discarded-input case also needed its test CGContext kept alive. The final fixture sets up a real font, keeps that context alive and resets frame clip state as production does. Actual glyph/shape inputs stay untouched under deferral; output is exact, including sanitizer and retry checks.
The text-scope fixture needed the existing initial-clear capability declaration and the production -fno-rtti option. Final optimized and sanitized scope checks execute successfully.

Disk exhaustion caused build, source-edit and shell-redirection failures. Completed old compiler input directories were archived losslessly, with every original file hash checked and restore instructions retained. Closed old incomplete Git temporary packs classified as garbage were removed; tracked source/history and measurement inputs were preserved. A temporary local gc.auto override did not prevent recurrence and was restored to its original value.

The timer worker fixture initially used dispatch_sync, which can run inline on the calling main thread. Final checks use an asynchronous worker and assert its actual thread, under both ARC and manual memory management.
The post-deferral sample is diagnostic only and uses a longer input sequence. It supplies no unprofiled optimization credit.

Some canonical run.json records do not recognize every new instrumentation flag. The explicit role field marks those attempts diagnostic; only unprofiled control/candidate pairs supply timing comparisons.

Timer and parallel-readback cohort controller exit three means the completed diagnostic found no input-window eligible work; the browser and memory guard exited zero. No candidate timing cohort was run.
